range: The project description identifies an ML-oriented columnar format emphasizing random access, vector search, versioning and integrations, with an aspirational de facto standard goal. Links delegate additional rules to Rust, Python, Java, protobuf and format-documentation guides. This description is not a benchmark or service guarantee.

Stable formats require backward and forward compatibility against released stable contracts. Exclusively unstable revisions are disposable and must not accumulate compatibility migrations/tests for prior unstable layouts. Intermediate branch/main states are not released compatibility constraints. Legacy paths no current writer emits are frozen: preserve reading, build new features in current paths, and avoid unrelated legacy refactors. Unavoidable shared-boundary edits must be isolated and covered by released historical fixtures.

Prescribed Rust commands include workspace check with tests/benches; workspace or targeted package tests; clippy --all --tests --benches with warnings denied; cargo fmt --all; nightly llvm-cov branch coverage (optionally HTML); and ci/coverage.py. Use repository profiles, release-with-debug for benchmarks/profiling, and release-no-lto only when appropriate for local debugging, IO-bound or compile-sensitive investigations. These are documented commands, not confirmed successful invocations or proof every named profile is defined in this checkout.

Language-specific environment instructions must precede tooling. Do not switch managers/toolchains merely because tooling is missing or slow. A command run outside the documented workflow is first an environment usage error; correct usage and rerun before reporting a dependency/tool failure.

Code/examples/comments use English and prioritize readability; comments explain non-obvious reasons. Remove stdout/debug prints in favor of logging. Add helpers only for real cognitive/duplication benefit, keep PRs focused, avoid collecting RecordBatch streams, and prefer RoaringBitmap to HashSet<u32>. These are maintainer rules, not claims that every existing file complies.

Keep Python/Java bindings thin and core validation in Rust. Maintain parameter names across languages. Preserve public signatures using deprecation plus new APIs. Replace mutually exclusive booleans with one mode/enum.

Names describe the value, avoid redundant domain prefixes, consistently use indices, use storage-neutral base terminology, and update every reference when renaming. Validate invalid/mutually exclusive options at boundaries without clamping; errors include relevant names, values, sizes and types.

Prefer standard/existing dependencies, intentional lock changes, documented pins for broken dependencies and optional feature gates/domain crates. Workspace dependency edits must update root, Python and JNI lockfiles, including cargo check against the excluded Python/JNI manifests; cargo-lock-sync is the stated offline enforcement hook. Actual hook implementation is pending analysis.

Every feature/bugfix requires tests. Local cases target under one second with small fixtures and split matrices, never weakened assertions/recall. Parameterize input-only differences with named rstest cases or pytest.parametrize; assert rather than print; extend existing tests; skipped tests require issue URLs. Dataset tests include multiple fragments; index cases cover null items/all-null/empty/null columns; vector creation must assert recall >=0.5. Compatibility fixtures live in test_data with datagen.py asserting writer version and copy_test_data_to_tmp for reads.

Public APIs need documentation/examples and links; hierarchical diagrams use ASCII; examples follow current signatures; MkDocs admonition bodies use four-space indentation; proofread comments/docs. The KB itself is external documentation, so these describe future repository editing obligations.
CLI/API-created issues require explicit bug/feature/performance labels because forms are bypassed. Titles use bug:/feature:/perf: with a workflow labeler as fallback, not a replacement for labels.

Before PR creation search for duplicates and inspect linked PR state/scope. Conventional Commit titles are enforced by commitlint workflow. Before PR creation/update run every touched language's prescribed lint, including full Rust fmt/clippy and Python uv-run lint; if blocked, state the reason in the PR summary. This KB task creates no PR and its no-network/read-only constraints remain in force.

Reviews prioritize scarce maintainer attention: concise P0/P1 severe correctness/performance/security findings, avoid repeating praise/change descriptions, and check naming/errors/tests. This review policy does not reduce the user's exhaustive KB scope.

The guide inherits root rules. Format doc changes require a PMC vote enforced by format-spec-vote; pair the spec/proto contract and only compilation-required library edits in one PR, implement separately afterward.

Keep format docs concise reference text; place code examples in user guides. Express file schemas as explicit PyArrow schema definitions, and use language-neutral JSON Schema/protobuf rather than Rust structures for general contracts. These rules coexist: schema definitions are expressly required even though illustrative code examples belong elsewhere.

Explain actual evolution mechanics (IDs/tombstones/rewrites), algorithms with parameters, precision, order, normalization and steps, and index file schemas plus navigation/entry-point/page-type distinctions. Naming an algorithm or deferring to an outside spec is insufficient. Bitmap index docs are the referenced pattern, pending their own analysis.
The guide inherits root standards and requires the ./mvnw wrapper rather than system mvn so Maven version selection is controlled.

Java sources live under java/src/main/java and Rust JNI under java/lance-jni. Group related options in Options/Params objects or builders; use typed enums with explicit Rust serialization rather than Java enum toString spelling and test each enum crossing. Public/IPC handles should be opaque protobuf-backed bytes rather than exposing internal data structures.
Prefer imports except ambiguity, JavaBean getXXX accessors for ecosystem compatibility, and Javadoc that repeats relevant Rust defaults/constraints/invariants so callers need no Rust source.
License, proto3 and lance.index.pb precede Any and index_old.proto imports. IndexType declares only VECTOR=0; this enum is not an exhaustive list of all index kinds in the repository.

Index has unique dataset index name=1, repeated indexed column names=2, build dataset_version=3, IndexType=4, and implementation oneof VectorIndex vector_index=5. Its shape describes this metadata envelope, not the newer generic Any detail registry.

Tensor.DataType enumerates BFLOAT16=0, FLOAT16=1, FLOAT32=2, FLOAT64=3, UINT8=4, UINT16=5, UINT32=6, UINT64=7. Tensor carries data_type=1, repeated uint32 shape=2, bytes data=3. The comments define shape dimensions but not byte order, strides, validation, or memory alignment.

IVF metadata stores repeated float centroids=1 (deprecated in prose, with the actual protobuf deprecated option commented out), repeated uint64 partition offsets=2, repeated uint32 record lengths=3, Tensor centroids_tensor=4, and optional double KMeans loss=5. Centroid shape is num_partitions by dimension. Implementations must decide compatibility precedence; this schema does not say what happens if both centroid forms are populated.

PQ records num_bits=1, num_sub_vectors=2, dimension=3, repeated float codebook=4, and Tensor codebook_tensor=5. Both codebook descriptions require dimension times 2^num_bits scalar values. This is metadata, not the sub-vector layout or distance implementation; no legal-bit-range validation appears.

TransformType declares OPQ=0. Transform stores matrix file position=1, repeated uint32 shape [rows,cols]=2, and transform type=3. Flat is an empty marker. These encode stage descriptions without executing a transformation.

DiskAnn carries spec=1, filename=2, r=3, alpha=4, capital-L field L=5, and repeated graph entry IDs=6. The schema supplies parameter names but not the graph algorithm or numeric bounds. VectorIndexStage.stage selects Flat=1, IVF=2, PQ=3, Transform=4, or DiskAnn=5; retaining order in the surrounding repeated stage list is essential to represent a pipeline. Ordered pipeline example: protos/index.proto:176-184.

VectorMetricType declares L2=0, Cosine=1, Dot=2, Hamming=3. VectorIndex stores spec_version=1, dimension=2, repeated stages=3, metric_type=4; its example composes IVF then PQ with 8 bits and 16 subvectors. The enum names do not specify normalization or squared-versus-unsquared numeric outputs.

VectorIndexDetails is stored in manifest index_details. metric_type=1 chooses metric; target_partition_size=2 uses zero for unset; optional HnswParameters=3 indicates an HNSW layer. Nested ProductQuantization has num_bits=1 and num_sub_vectors=2; ScalarQuantization has num_bits=1; RabitQuantization has num_bits=1 and RotationType=2 with FAST=0, MATRIX=1; FlatCompression is empty and means stored unquantized vectors.

HnswParameters has max_connections=1 (M, outgoing-edge bound: more improves recall at memory/build cost), construction_ef=2 (dynamic candidate list size during construction), and max_level=3. Defaults, legality checks, and exact complexity are not given.

JsonIndexDetails stores JSON path string=1 and google.protobuf.Any target_details=2, allowing nested index-kind details. BloomFilterIndexDetails, RTreeIndexDetails, and FMIndexDetails are empty markers. Empty metadata messages do not imply empty index files or lack of implementation options.

MinHashLshIndexDetails is explicitly experimental: incompatible detail/file changes may require rebuilding the index, not rewriting data, and the feature may be removed if stabilization fails. Every segment must share identical details, query signatures must be comparable, and both index files repeat serialized details in schema metadata to detect mismatches. Readers validate every field before allocation or file read. num_hashes=1 is in [1,4096] and divisible by num_bands; num_bands=2 is in [1,256]; each band covers num_hashes/num_bands consecutive values.

Transaction exists to rebuild a manifest on retry and determine compatibility after conflict. read_version uint64=1 is the snapshot used for planning/evaluating predicates; uuid string=2 identifies the transaction; tag string=3 is described as optional but lacks scalar presence; transaction_properties string map=4 reserves __lance_commit_message. These fields are not the newly assigned commit version.

TableIdentifier has string uri tag 1, uint64 version tag 2, optional string manifest_etag tag 3, optional bytes serialized_manifest tag 4, and string-to-string storage_options map tag 5. The documented fast mode supplies URI plus serialized manifest so the executor can skip reading a manifest; the lightweight mode supplies URI, version, and ETag so the executor loads it. Presence distinguishes absent optional ETag/manifest from an explicitly present empty value. The schema does not encode mode exclusivity or precedence when both reconstruction forms are supplied; it declares no validation of URI or storage options. Changing tags or presence loses wire meaning.

VectorApproxMode defines Normal=0 (all RQ bits, u8 lookup tables), Fast=1 (one RQ bit even for a multibit index), and Accurate=2 (all RQ bits, u16 lookup tables to reduce estimator quantization error). The documented effect is restricted to RQ-quantized indices such as IVF_RQ; other index types ignore it. Normal is the zero-valued wire enum variant, not an independently verified application default.

CoveringProjection wraps repeated int32 field_ids tag 1. Its message presence represents three states that an unwrapped repeated field could not preserve: absent means no narrowing computed and all declared covering columns materialized; present-empty means no covering values; present-nonempty means exactly the selected dataset field IDs. Replacing it with a bare list would conflate absent and empty.

VectorQueryProto carries Arrow IPC query-vector bytes tag 1 (the comment explicitly allows Float16/32/64 and UInt8 among others), column tag 2, k tag 3, optional float lower/upper bounds tags 4/5, optional uint32 minimum/maximum probes 6/7, ef 8, refine_factor 9, optional VectorMetricType 10, bool use_index 11, optional float dist_q_c 12, and optional int32 query_parallelism 13. Absent metric means use the index default. Numeric valid ranges, bound inclusivity, and dist_q_c semantics are not defined here; the declarations do not validate them.

ANNIvfSubIndexExecProto serializes query tag 1, TableIdentifier tag 2, repeated lance.table.IndexMetadata indices tag 3, and prefilter_type tag 4. Nested PreFilterType is NONE=0, FILTERED_ROW_IDS=1, SCALAR_INDEX_QUERY=2. DataFusion codecs carry the actual prefilter child plan through children()/with_new_children(); this enum selects the PreFilterSource reconstruction variant. The child must not be mistaken for embedded protobuf bytes in this message.

ANNIvfPartitionExecProto is the IVF centroid routing node's serialized form: query tag 1, TableIdentifier tag 2, repeated string index_uuids tag 3. It carries UUID strings rather than the IndexMetadata list of the sub-index node. No child plan field or extra routing algorithm is declared.

BTreeIndexDetails, BitmapIndexDetails, LabelListIndexDetails, and NGramIndexDetails are empty type markers. ZoneMapIndexDetails.rows_per_zone is optional uint64 tag 1; absent represents old datasets and prevents seed-writer creation, not an implicit numeric zone size.

ZoneMap has_null_bitmap optional bool tag 3 enables exact null-row address tracking. Absent/false use legacy approximate zone statistics for IS NULL; true makes IS NULL exact and supports IS NOT NULL without a full scan. The closing brace ends ZoneMap and the next declaration begins InvertedIndexDetails.

RowIdSequence.segments tag 1 is an ordered repeated U64Segment sequence. Segment encodings favor sorted and differently sparse IDs. Nested U64Segment.Range uses uint64 start=1 inclusive and end=2 exclusive; empty or reversed-range validation is not encoded here.

EncodedU64Array contains U16Array(base uint64=1, offsets bytes=2), U32Array(base uint64=1, offsets bytes=2), and U64Array(values bytes=2). Offsets are unsigned 16- or 32-bit deltas; bytes avoid unsupported uint16 and uint32 varint overhead, while full u64 bytes avoid varints. The array oneof selects u16_array=1, u32_array=2, or u64_array=3. Endianness, alignment, and overflow checks are not stated, so exact byte decoding requires the Rust implementation. The heading calls this bitpacked, whereas declarations explicitly provide fixed-width byte variants; retain that distinction.

RowDatasetVersionSequence stores repeated RowDatasetVersionRun runs=1 for runs of equal dataset versions. Each run carries U64Segment span=1 and uint64 version=2. The span comment describes the number of consecutive rows, but its declared type is a segment rather than a scalar count; do not replace it with a count or assume how it is interpreted without checking the converter.

The opening historical-looking layout diagram lists encoded chunks, indices, chunk-position matrix, optional manifest, metadata, i64 metadata position, version pair and LANC. It is not the newer file2 footer diagram and should not be applied to every current file. UUID is a message with bytes uuid=1 documented as exactly 16 bytes; no validation is implemented in protobuf.

Manifest carries repeated lance.file.Field fields=1 including nested fields, repeated DataFragment fragments=2, uint64 version=3, uint64 version_aux_data=4, and bytes-valued schema_metadata map=5. fragment_tree=22 replaces the inline fragment list for tree tables: fragments must be empty and bit 12 set in both feature words so unaware readers do not see an empty dataset. Auxiliary data is version-specific, not inherited, and not loaded by default on query.

base_paths repeated BasePath=18 resolves imported, shallow-cloned or multi-tier files; example resolves ID zero as base/data/file.path and IDs increase from zero. branch optional string=20 uses absence for main. BasePath has id uint32=1, optional alias name=2 (source tag for shallow clone), is_dataset_root bool=3 distinguishing dataset roots with data/_deletions subdirectories from direct file directories, and absolute path string=4 parsed directly. The comment refers to lance.file.File/DeletionFile, but actual declarations are lance.table.DataFile/DeletionFile (protos/fragment_metadata.proto:6-6; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:90-90; protos/fragment_metadata.proto:257-257).
VersionAuxData is loaded on demand and has metadata map<string,bytes>=3. Its absence/default loading policy comes from Manifest.version_aux_data; it is not table configuration.

IndexMetadata.uuid message=1 is unique across dataset versions; fields repeated int32=2 refers to logical Field IDs and preserves key order; name string=3 is unique within a version; dataset_version uint64=4 is the build version. With manifest bit 13 fields contains keys only; otherwise legacy carried values form the trailing suffix. The same bytes have different interpretation depending on the manifest flag, making atomic migration mandatory.

IndexFile has index-directory-relative path string=1 and size_bytes uint64=2. IndexSection contains repeated IndexMetadata indices=1 for one dataset version. A comment records VectorIndexDetails and renamed HnswParameters moving to index.proto; it is not another declaration.

FragmentReuseIndexDetails.content chooses InlineContent inline=1 or ExternalFile external=2; comment threshold is below 200 KB inline, otherwise external InlineContent bytes, with exact unit/threshold selection to verify in code. InlineContent stores historical Version legacy_versions=1 and new Transition transitions=2 requiring index_version=1. Transition has source FragmentDigests=1 in scan order including deleted rows, destinations=2 in label order with creation counts, and exactly one ordered_compaction=3 or stable_partition=4 mapping. New safe backward-compatible mappings, including scan fallback, need no version bump; unsafe ones do. Ordered compaction concatenates surviving source rows in scan order then splits; stable partition distributes sequential source rows by destination label.

The MemWAL section introduces ShardStatus ACTIVE=0 and SEALED=1. Drop-table two-phase commit seals a shard to refuse claims reversibly, then deletes on commit or returns ACTIVE on rollback. ShardManifest documents exactly one active writer per shard; shard_id UUID=11 is v4, version uint64=1 matches manifest filename, shard_spec_id uint32=10 is immutable at creation with zero for manual/unmanaged shards, and shard_field_entries repeated=14 stores raw Arrow scalar bytes keyed by field ID and interpreted by ShardingSpec.result_type. The comment explicitly gives little-endian int32 and raw UTF-8 examples.

ShardFieldEntry has field_id string=1 matching ShardingField.field_id and value bytes=2 in raw little-endian Arrow representation; matching result_type gives the data type. There is no self-describing per-value type tag here.

SsTable is an immutable flushed MemTable stored as a Lance dataset. generation uint64=1 and shard-relative path string=2 identify it. Optional in_memory_bytes=3 estimates accounted buffer windows, excluding reader array structure and requiring headroom; absent means unknown, not zero. Optional physical_rows=4 includes older primary-key duplicates masked by its deletion vector. Optional primary_key_bytes=5 sums key-column payload over all physical rows, is not per-row/encoded-sort-key size, and is also absent without a primary key. Treating these estimates as hard bounds or defaults as zero risks underbudgeting.

CompactedSsTable has shard_id UUID=1 and generation uint64=2 for latest compaction into base data. IndexCatchupProgress has base index_name=1 (must match maintained_indexes) and caught_up_generations repeated=2. An absent shard means unknown progress, so retain SSTables and schedule repair; it does not mean fully caught up or safe to delete.

MemWalIndexDetails centralizes configuration, base compaction progress, and shard snapshots. Writers read configuration; snapshots are point-in-time optimizations, while readers requiring current shards list directories and latest shard manifests. Background refresh does not make snapshots authoritative mutable shard state. Snapshot Lance-file schema lists shard_id utf8, shard_spec_id uint32, typed shard_field_{id}. snapshot_ts_millis int64=1 and num_shards uint32=2 describe it; optional inline_snapshots bytes=3 holds Lance bytes for small counts. The threshold example 100 is explicitly implementation-defined, not a specified constant.

writer_config_defaults map<string,string>=11 persists common process/restart defaults, while each ShardWriterConfig may override at runtime without persisting those overrides. ShardingSpec has spec_id uint32=1 unique within index and never reused, plus repeated ShardingField fields=2. Concrete map keys and defaults are not enumerated here.

ShardingField declares field_id string=1, repeated int32 source_ids=2, optional transform string=3 (examples identity/year/bucket), optional DataFusion SQL expression string=4, result_type string=5 as Arrow type name, parameters string map=6 (example num_buckets). transform and expression are mutually exclusive by comment but are separate optional fields, so an implementation must reject both being present. Valid transforms, SQL restrictions, and result-type validation are not enforced here.

Structural encodings are called layouts. RepDefLayer records each peeled list/struct layer's interpretation: UNSPECIFIED=0 is invalid/debug; ALL_VALID_ITEM=1, ALL_VALID_LIST=2, NULLABLE_ITEM=3, NULLABLE_LIST=4 (null but no empty lists), EMPTYABLE_LIST=5 (empty but no null), NULL_AND_EMPTY_LIST=6. ITEM includes primitives or structs. Null and empty list layers are distinct even when neither emits a child value.

MiniBlockLayout targets small values where per-value transposition is expensive; comments describe sector-sized compressed chunks and bulk compression tradeoffs. Its prose also says an entire page must be read, which requires checking against the actual mini-block reader rather than treating it as established scheduling behavior. Optional-in-presence rep_compression=1 and def_compression=2 describe levels, value_compression=3 values, dictionary=4 optional dictionary encoding, num_dictionary_items uint64=5, and repeated RepDefLayer layers=6. Omitted rep/def/dictionary messages mean those components are absent.

FullZipLayout targets large values where transposition cost is relatively low, zipping buffers. bits_rep uint32=1 and bits_def=2 use zero for none. details oneof selects fixed bits_per_value=3 or variable bits_per_offset=4; prose favors byte multiples for large values but does not declare a validation rule. num_items uint32=5 and num_visible_items=6 are separately stored; value_compression=7 and layers=8 describe values/structure. These counts are uint32, unlike MiniBlock's uint64 num_items.

SparseLayout stores Arrow structure in layer-local slot domains, ordered outermost to innermost, with independently readable compressed value chunks. Fields: value_compression=1, num_buffers uint64=2 excluding structure, num_items uint64=3, num_visible_items uint64=4, has_large_chunk bool=5 choosing u32 versus u16 chunk-local value-buffer sizes, structural_layers repeated=6. num_items equals visible leaf slots plus one placeholder per list slot without children; null primitive slots remain visible slots. Thus a 100-slot primitive with 30 nulls has both counts 100. Structural layers can be empty for a flat non-null leaf when scheduling domain equals visible items.

Domains are [0,num_slots) coordinates. Outermost means page rows; each layer's child domain is the next layer's parent; the final domain has num_visible_items slots. SparseStructuralLayer.layer requires exactly one validity=1, list=2, or fixed_size_list=3 arm. SparseValidityLayer preserves num_slots uint64=1 across parent/child and records SparseValiditySet validity=2. The requirement for exactly one is a semantic constraint; oneof alone also admits unset.

SparseListLayer uses num_slots=1, num_child_slots=2, SparsePositionSet non_empty_positions=3, SparseCountSet counts=4, validity=5. Counts are positive and parallel non-empty positions; valid parents absent from that set are empty. SparseFixedSizeListLayer uses num_slots=1, dimension=2, validity=3, with child cardinality num_slots*dimension. Parent nullness and child coordinates are separate, and multiplication/consistency checks belong to implementation.

SparseValiditySet has Meaning meaning=1 and SparsePositionSet positions=2. Meaning UNSPECIFIED=0, NULL_POSITIONS=1 (stored positions null, all others valid), VALID_POSITIONS=2 (inverse). Empty and All position markers are separate empty messages. SparsePositionRange has uint64 start=1 and length=2; it is a start/count representation, not start/end.

SparsePositionSet.positions selects explicit CompressiveEncoding=1 for delta-compressed u64 positions, nonempty contiguous range=2, all=3, or empty=4. num_positions uint64=5 records semantic cardinality for every alternative. Explicit cardinality, range length, all-domain size, and empty-zero consistency are obligations implied by the contract, not validated by the schema.

SparseCountEmpty is empty. SparseCountConstant.value uint64=1 is the common positive child count. SparseCountSet.counts selects explicit compressed u64 counts=1 with cardinality inherited from the containing position set, constant=2, or empty=3 allowed only when no nonempty list slots exist. No separate count-list length is stored.

ConstantLayout generalizes prior all-null semantics at file_version >=2.2 to any page whose visible values are the same scalar. Repetition/definition buffers may still be required to explain visibility/null kinds. layers repeated=5; optional inline_value bytes=6 must be absent for all-null pages, at most 32 bytes when present, and only for a non-null scalar representable by one fixed-width Arrow value buffer without offsets or children. This is a structural page constant, distinct from the compressive Constant message.

BlobLayout externalizes large binary payloads and stores position/size descriptions. (position=0,size=0) means empty; (nonzero position,size=0) means null and position carries repdef. inner_layout PageLayout=1 encodes descriptions with exactly one all-valid-item repdef layer, while outer layers repeated=2 describe original structure. Conflating zero-length null and empty corrupts semantics.

PageLayout.layout selects MiniBlockLayout=1, ConstantLayout=2, FullZipLayout=3, BlobLayout=4, SparseLayout=5. The sparse arm explicitly requires file version 2.3 or later. Constant's non-null extension and MiniBlock large-chunk extension have their own 2.2 statements; the file's 2.1 name is not a universal gate (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:126-127; protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:288-290).

CompressionScheme enumerates UNSPECIFIED=0, LZ4=1, ZSTD=2. BufferCompression.scheme=1 and optional signed level=2 apply to a whole buffer. Absent level uses a scheme-specific default whose number is not stated. General buffer compression makes a parent opaque even if its ordinary encoding is transparent. Higher levels generally trade CPU for compression, but no measured complexity is given.

Flat takes fixed-width data to one buffer, with positive bits_per_value uint64=1 (not necessarily byte multiple) and optional BufferCompression data=2. Variable takes variable-width data to compressed offsets CompressiveEncoding=1 plus a value buffer with optional BufferCompression values=2. The prose calls them transparent/uncompressed leaves, but their declared optional buffer compression invokes the opacity rule above; readers must interpret those comments conditionally rather than ignore data/values compression (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:385-407).

Compressive Constant accepts any block, stores optional bytes value=1 in metadata, emits no output buffers, and leaves literal encoding as a TODO. OutOfLineBitpacking reduces fixed-width values by removing redundant upper bits; uncompressed_bits_per_value uint64=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=3 describe the result. Prose says compressed width is fixed and stored in this message, but there is no direct compressed-width scalar here; it must be recovered through nested encoding/implementation. Do not copy the old package's compressed_bits_per_value tag into this schema.

InlineBitpacking stores original width uint64=1 and optional BufferCompression values=2. Compressed widths live inline per chunk, allowing variation to tolerate outliers; the encoding is opaque and turns a fixed-width data block into one buffer. Chunk header byte layout is not specified here.

Fsst uses one page-wide symbol table stored in bytes symbol_table=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=2 for the transformed variable-width block. The contract calls the transform transparent. It does not specify symbol-table serialization or the FSST algorithm itself.

Dictionary maps a data block of any kind to a same-kind dictionary and fixed-width indices, recursively compressed by indices=1 and items=2; num_dictionary_items uint32=3 stores dictionary size. It is opaque unless dictionary content is considered metadata. Index widths, null conventions, invalid-index errors, and metadata placement require implementation evidence.

Rle emits same-kind run values and fixed-width run lengths, represented by CompressiveEncoding values=1 and run_lengths=2. It is opaque unless lengths are metadata. Unlike the older Rle declaration, it does not directly carry bits_per_value; the value-width description lives in the nested encoding.

FixedSizeList is a transparent structural flattening transform within the compressive tree, converting wide/fewer fixed-width items to narrower/more items without itself compressing. items_per_value uint64=1 is this layer's dimension, values CompressiveEncoding=2 encodes flattened output, and has_validity bool=3 records validity buffer presence. This differs from SparseFixedSizeListLayer's parent/child-domain description.

PackedStruct is the legacy fixed-width form: row-by-row concatenation of fixed-width children, repeated uint64 bits_per_value=1 specifying each contribution and CompressiveEncoding values=2. VariablePackedStruct is a 2.2 extension with repeated FieldEncoding fields=1 in struct order. Each child is independently compressed before row-major transposition, preserving field compression boundaries but disabling mini-block compression. FieldEncoding.value=1 describes compression and layout selects bits_per_value uint64=2 or bits_per_length uint64=3 for variable-length prefixes. The prose says readers prefer this form when present and fall back to legacy; the enclosing union makes the concrete selection explicit (protos/encodings_v2_1.proto:658-675).

General wraps the output of its inner encoding, unlike other encodings' input-oriented composition. In mini-block layout it compresses the whole mini-block; in full-zip it compresses individual values. In the FSST/Variable/bitpacked-offset example, compression can apply to offsets alone, value bytes alone, or the combined mini-block, or combinations. General has BufferCompression compression=1 and CompressiveEncoding values=3, preserving data-block kind. Choosing placement changes random-access granularity and what must be decompressed together, as an inference from the documented units.

ByteStreamSplit transposes fixed-width values into byte streams without reducing size by itself, then recursively encodes them using CompressiveEncoding values=1. It is opaque and keeps fixed-width block kind. The prose's attribution of upper bits to mantissa is not sufficient to define a numeric representation; this KB retains the text but requires implementation-level bit mapping before giving an exact algorithm.

CompressiveEncoding.compression selects flat=1, variable=2, constant=3, out_of_line_bitpacking=4, inline_bitpacking=5, fsst=6, dictionary=7, rle=8, byte_stream_split=9, general=10, fixed_size_list=11, packed_struct=12, variable_packed_struct=13. These tags and nested types are different from the older ArrayEncoding union. No unknown/unset variant handling is implemented here.
The title scopes the guide to protobufs and the root AGENTS.md link incorporates cross-language standards.

Persisted-format protobuf changes require a PMC vote enforced by format-spec-vote. Keep the schema change with its matching docs/src/format change and compilation-only library adjustments, then implement separately. ann.proto, filtered_read.proto, and table_identifier.proto are execution wire contracts whose implementation changes belong together and do not require this format vote or format-doc change.

Stable persisted contracts preserve existing field numbers and backwards compatibility. Exclusively unstable schemas need not preserve earlier unstable revisions, but shared stable usage must be checked first. Execution-wire field numbers stay compatible unless all producers and consumers upgrade atomically.

Use optional for absent-versus-zero presence, mapping to Rust Option and has_* accessors. Prefer structured messages, operation-specific field scope, one representation of each fact, and parallel sequences when keys already exist elsewhere.

Document both presence states and precise terms. Multiline comments use block syntax for folding, single-line comments use //. ci/check_proto_comments.py, pre-commit, and the Protobuf lint workflow enforce this convention; --fix can rewrite offenders.

DataFragment groups column files for the same rows. Missing schema columns within a fragment read as all-null. id=1 is dataset-unique, files=2 is the file list, deletion_file=3 identifies tombstones, and overlays=11 must be empty unless manifest flag 64 is set. The overlay list is ordered: later entries win ties in committed_version for the same cell. The inline-tombstone bitmap question is a TODO, not an implemented arm.

DataFile.path=1 is dataset-relative. fields=2 lists signed field IDs: in-memory -1 is unassigned and must not persist; -2 is tombstoned; all negatives are reserved system values rather than schema fields and projection skips them, including -3/-4/-5 lineage IDs. The v1 comment assigns IDs by file position plus existing maximum and counts nested struct/list fields but one ID for a fixed-size list; v1 IDs are sorted but need not be contiguous. For v2 the field ID cannot determine the physical column because encoding choices change column count, so use column_indices. The example's wording about second fragments versus files is retained as a comment-level account, not confirmed allocator behavior.

DataOverlayFile stores replacement cell values without rewriting base files. Consult overlays newest to oldest, falling through to base when absent; deletions take precedence and suppress overlay values. data_file=1 contains one value column per declared field, no row-offset key column. Value position equals the count of coverage bits below the physical offset (zero-based rank), and columns can differ in length. coverage selects shared_offset_bitmap bytes=2 (32-bit Roaring offsets shared by every field) or FieldCoverage=4 (independent field offsets). Dense UPDATE and sparse MERGE are motivating examples, not different file types.

FieldCoverage.offset_bitmaps=1 is a repeated bytes list with one 32-bit Roaring bitmap per data_file.fields entry in the same order. A present offset whose value is NULL overrides to NULL; an absent offset falls through to base. A sparse NULL update must not be encoded by simply omitting the offset.

DeletionFile path is {root}/_deletions/{fragment_id}-{read_version}-{id}.{extension}. Nested DeletionFileType is ARROW_ARRAY=0 (one Arrow IPC batch containing one Int32Array column, .arrow) or BITMAP=1 (Roaring bitmap, .bin). Comments motivate sparse versus dense selection but provide no threshold. Fields are file_type=1, read_version=2, concurrent-writer differentiating id=3, num_deleted_rows=4, and optional base_id=7 for Manifest.base_paths. Deletions operate on offsets, not stable logical IDs.

RowLineageColumn is an empty marker. Exactly one DataFragment.files entry carries the relevant reserved field ID (-3 row ID, -4 creation version, -5 update version), and its column_indices identifies the column. It may share a data file or be separate; values are non-null uint64, exactly physical_rows long in physical order. Only v2 data files support this mapping; v1 datasets keep sequences inline. Metadata is stored once in files, not repeated in the marker.

ExternalFile is a table-relative path=1 plus byte offset=2 and size=3, documented for fragment reuse index details rather than the removed external lineage arms. FragmentTreeMetadata.layout currently has one tree=1 alternative; it selects the fragment storage layout. Removed external lineage arms: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:74-81.

FragmentTree selects inline_root=1 or root_uuid bytes=2. UUID must be exactly 16 display-order bytes and resolves to _bt/root/{lowercase hyphenated UUID}.root under this dataset. mutations_since_root=3 carries mutations absent from that root; next_action_sequence=4 is the next unused sequence for this version. FragmentTreeRoot stores children=1, buffer=2, and next_action_sequence=3 meaning the first action not represented by the root. Confusing root and version watermarks risks replaying or skipping mutations.

FragmentTreeChild routing is ordered by min_key and owns [min_key,next min_key), with the final upper bound inherited. path=1 is relative to resolved dataset; optional base_id=2 inherits the containing object's dataset when absent and otherwise matches Manifest.base_paths, including valid ID zero. min_key=3 need not exist in the child. num_keys=4, total_rows=7, and visible_rows=10 include the object's buffered mutations; height=5 counts edges to leaves, num_children=6 direct children, both zero for leaves; object_size=8 is stored byte length. materialized_through_action_sequence=9 records a leaf's fully applied watermark with no qualifying mutations above it, zero meaning none; interiors must use zero.

FragmentTreeNode holds children=1 and buffered mutations=2. FragmentTreeMutation holds action_sequence=1, FragmentAction action=2, and signed after-minus-before aggregate deltas fragment_count_delta=3, total_rows_delta=4, visible_rows_delta=5. Signed deltas preserve removals and deletions; these are validated changes by contract, not validation code.

FragmentAction.action oneof selects complete upsert_fragment=1, remove_fragment ID=2, AddDataFile=3, RemoveDataFile=4, AddDeletionFile=5, ClearDeletionFile=6, or ReplaceDataFile=7. Upsert replaces the entire fragment and covers changes lacking narrower actions, including overlays, version sequences, and row IDs. Treating it as a partial patch would retain obsolete state.

AddDataFile(frag_id=1,file=2) appends to ordered files. RemoveDataFile(frag_id=1,path=2) removes every matching path while preserving order of others. AddDeletionFile(frag_id=1,deletion_file=2) and ClearDeletionFile(frag_id=1) carry deletion changes. Missing-fragment handling and validation errors are not specified here.

ReplaceDataFile carries frag_id=1, expected_path=2, path=3, file_size_bytes=4, optional base_id=5. Replace only the first expected-path match, changing path/size/base while retaining column mapping and file version. An absent base inherits the dataset resolved for the tree object or version manifest containing the mutation; present base matches Manifest.base_paths. This differs deliberately from RemoveDataFile's all-match rule. Supporting all-match rule: protos/fragment_metadata.proto:428-432.

spawn_cpu closures must compute and return without channel waits, IO, locks, block_on or blocking APIs. On <=3 CPUs the pool may have one worker, so blocked work can deadlock the pool. Keep waits outside in async code and dispatch only substantial (~100 microseconds+) CPU work. This is a policy/explanation requiring comparison with cpu.rs, not a measured threshold or a blanket statement about every executor.

Builder option methods use with_, APIs prefer Into/AsRef, internals prefer pub(crate), public re-exports define the surface, and enums/typed structs replace magic numbers/unstructured maps. Keep physical RowAddr and stable RowId distinct; use RowAddress helpers and Roaring/RowAddrTreeMap selections. User counts subtract deletions; traits stay minimal; schema introspection must not materialize rows. Persistent formats are stable/versioned; Arrow access uses typed accessors (optional variants unless type proven); local IO writes use single syscalls instead of cloud multipart machinery.

Fallible library paths return contextual Result errors rather than panics/unwraps; use NotSupported instead of TODO/unimplemented, classify errors by cause, checked arithmetic for IDs/counters, debug assertions for non-safety invariants, and explicit handling of impossible states. A subsequent narrower rule permits expect with a reason only when unavoidable; this is not encouragement to bypass the earlier fallible-path prohibition. Warn for cleanup failures/silent no-ops, avoid duplicate warning-before-error, reject missing required config rather than defaulting, and advance/bind parallel iterators exactly once before skipping work.

Only truly unused bindings use underscore prefixes; booleans use is_/has_ and choose a desired zero/default state (disable_* for default-enabled behavior). Names describe actual scope rather than a broader operation.

Tests use record_batch! or gen_batch setup, try_into_batch for scans, plain memory:// storage, and assertions on both error variant and text. These rules specify meaningful tests without asserting any current suite passes.

new_arrow constructs an ArrowField then invokes TryFrom. data_type reconstructs List/LargeList using children[0], fixed-size-list-of-struct by parsing the last logical-string component with expect and taking children[0], Struct from all children, and Map from children[0] with sorted=false; other logical strings parse through DataType::try_from(...).unwrap(). Field Display prints id, name and logical type, optional Debug dictionary metadata and recursively formatted children, with a trailing comma/space after each child. It omits parent_id, nullability, encoding, most metadata and key-position members, so Display output is not a full serialized schema or equality key.

TryFrom<&ArrowField> clones metadata and removes lance:field_id. A present value must parse as i32 or returns Error::invalid_input; parsed negatives clamp to -1 via max(-1), absent means -1. No trimming occurs. Struct recursively converts all children, List/LargeList convert one, and FixedSizeList stores a Field child only when the Arrow element is Struct. Other scalar fixed-size-list children are encoded in logical_type. The imported metadata field ID is intentionally absent from retained metadata.

Constructed Field uses parent_id=-1, original name/nullability, converted children, dictionary=None and parsed positions. Encoding selection uses original Arrow datatype: fixed stride=>Plain, binary-like=>VarBinary, Dictionary=>Dictionary, List/LargeList/Map=>Plain for offsets, otherwise None. V2/JSON logical-type overrides do not independently recompute this choice. Owned ArrowField TryFrom delegates to borrowed conversion; it adds no validation.

CPU_RUNTIME starts as a null AtomicPtr<Runtime>; RUNTIME_INSTALLED and ATFORK_INSTALLED start false. They are private process-global state. Published runtimes are boxed and intentionally leaked; no shutdown/drop path is provided here.

global_cpu_runtime()->&'static Runtime loops: SeqCst load pointer, return unsafe shared reference when non-null, otherwise fetch_or(true) on installation flag to elect one initializer; other callers yield their OS thread and retry. extern C child-after-fork callback resets CPU_RUNTIME to null and RUNTIME_INSTALLED to false with SeqCst. It leaves ATFORK_INSTALLED true and does not drop the inherited runtime, avoiding arbitrary destructor execution in that callback. Next pool access in the child initializes a fresh runtime. The implementation does not install a parent/before-fork callback or prove safety of arbitrary forking application code. Publication and hook registration are at rust/lance-core/src/utils/tokio.rs:95-134.

On non-Windows, install_atfork invokes unsafe libc::pthread_atfork(None,None,Some(callback)); its return status is ignored. On Windows the same private name is a no-op. Registration failure is therefore not surfaced, and this implementation is platform-dependent.

Private x86 module contains check_flag(x:usize,position:u32)->bool and pub-in-private-module has_avx512_f16_support()/has_avx512(). FP16 detection first requires has_avx512(), then uses unsafe __cpuid(7) and tests EDX bit 23; has_avx512 uses is_x86_feature_detected!(avx512f). The CPUID instruction is architecture-gated and the feature gate precedes the raw bit test; downstream kernel safety still depends on callers. allow(unused_unsafe) accommodates toolchains differing on intrinsic safety. External links are comments, not fetched evidence. These helpers are not publicly reachable through the private module.

Provenance comments cite a third-party implementation. On aarch64 macOS the private module's has_neon_f16_support returns true with a platform-support assumption; no runtime auxiliary-vector query occurs.

On aarch64 Linux, the helper calls unsafe libc::getauxval(AT_HWCAP) and tests libc::HWCAP_FPHP. It does not return or inspect errno; a false bit produces false. This is a platform capability query, not an unsafe memory dereference in this source.

On aarch64 Windows the helper returns false and includes an issue URL without an inline explanation or TODO. The linked issue was not accessed, so the reason for disabling this helper is not established here. The aarch64 initializer consequently selects None on this target (rust/lance-core/src/utils/cpu.rs:171-180); selected tier is Lance dispatch policy rather than a hardware inventory.

The private loongarch64 module exposes internally reachable has_lsx_support and has_lasx_support, each using unsafe getauxval(AT_HWCAP) and its respective libc feature bit. The module has an architecture cfg, not an additional OS cfg; this file alone does not prove every loongarch operating system compiles.

On aarch64 Android the helper returns false. Only the explicit platform combinations above supply aarch64 helper modules; support for other operating systems must not be inferred from the broad aarch64 call site.

Private test module imports the API and rstest. simd_info_exposes_tier checks ARCH and cached tier identity. x86-only simd_info_features_include_baseline checks sse2; the complementary non-x86 test checks an empty raw feature vector. These are host-conditioned tests, not simulated cross-platform coverage.

Unconditionally public utility submodules are address, aimd, assume, backoff, bit, blob, bloomfilter, cpu, deletion, fragment_reuse, futures, hash, io_stats, parse, path, row_addr_remap, stable_partition, tempfile, testing, tokio, tracing. No cfg gates are attached here; in particular testing is publicly declared outside cfg(test), though its contents may have their own conditions. Module names alone are not behavioral contracts for their implementation.
